Curving Skirting Board

I built a house with curved walls. Skirting board took one look and declined. So: build a steam box, bend the timber, fix it while it still remembers the shape.

Small domestic detail on the surface. Underneath: geometry, moisture, heat, timing, and a real chance of snapping it at the last moment.

Watch the steam box See the wall fit
BUILD SPEC OAK / STEAM
Timber
Oak, 18mm thick and 120mm tall. Oak steams well, which is most of the reason it is oak.
Steam box
A length of ventilation pipe, insulated, fed by a wallpaper steamer. It looks like a piece of improvised nonsense on the terrace and it worked properly first time.
Steam time
Twenty to thirty minutes a length. Less than the usual hour-per-inch advice, and enough.
Bend radius
Over a 2.4m length the far end finishes about a metre off the line of the near end — roughly a 2.7m radius, set by the wall rather than by choice.
Springback
None to speak of, because it never got the chance: straight out of the box and screwed to the wall while it was still persuadable.
Fixing method
Screwed into timber battens where there were battens, and into rawlplugs where the run was straight onto the wall.

What went wrong

Nothing, which was not the expected outcome. Steam bending has a reputation for splitting expensive timber at the last moment, and the whole job was set up around that risk — box ready, wall ready, screws and clamps waiting, because the clock starts the moment the timber comes out. Not a single length cracked.

What I would change

Nothing. The one time I get to write that.

Fit

Onto the curved wall

The constraint

Straight timber, curved house.

The wall was curved because the house was designed that way. The skirting had to follow it, which turned a trim job into a bending problem.

The method

Heat buys time.

Steam makes the timber briefly compliant. The clock starts the moment it leaves the box, so the wall, tools and fixings all have to be ready and waiting.

The house

The drawings live in a git repo, obviously

This sits inside the wider house-build story, including the drawings and design work in the ChadHouse repo. Curved walls are lovely. They also send you outside to build strange foil tubes.

The payoff

The finished detail

Done well, visitors see skirting board and think nothing at all. Weeks of work, invisible on purpose.
